where: data/shared/evidence/benchmarks.csv; data/catalog/source_documents.csv; every Climate TRACE row
what: Climate TRACE is registered by its API PATH, not by a dataset release. 'v7' is the URL segment https://api.climatetrace.org/v7. No held payload carries a dataset version field; sources/ClimateTRACE/climatetrace_waste_PAK_SUMMARY.json records only "api": "https://api.climatetrace.org/v7". A single free-text note says 'v7.1.9 where the note says so', which is not a per-row field.
consequence: The six Climate TRACE agriculture rows in national_benchmark_comparison.csv cannot be reproduced: no dataset release, no retrieval date, no held file, no digest. Climate TRACE restates history between releases, so the comparison is not re-runnable and a future disagreement cannot be attributed.
suggested_fix: Record the release the API reports in its own metadata, retain the country-by-subsector payload with a digest, and pull the NATIVE-GAS rows the API already serves so the CO2e inversion in MC-04..MC-06 becomes unnecessary.

what: The same file (sha256 52637aa4...) is called 'Climate TRACE v7 power assets' by the catalog and 'Climate TRACE v6 API' by the README, which records the call as api.climatetrace.org/v6/assets.
consequence: The power asset snapshot came from a DIFFERENT API generation than the aviation and waste snapshots, and nothing in the registry says so.
suggested_fix: Record the actual endpoint per file.

what: One CRT zip (sha256 afba70d1...) carries two different UNFCCC document URLs: 655653 in the sector manifests, 645241 in the catalog. 645241 is the BTR1's own record.
consequence: A reader following the catalog URL lands on the BTR1, not the CRT.
suggested_fix: Pick the correct record and make the other a cross-reference.

what: Each row points at 'data/manifests/source_manifest.csv', a path that does not exist; the curated manifests are at data/catalog/manifests/. That file covers apcma, fao_crop_calendar, ipcc, nfdc, ocac, ogra and pbs only - there is no EDGAR, GEM, FAOSTAT, land, emep or epa_ap42 row.
consequence: For the comparator families this registry covers, retrieved_at_utc, source_url, coverage and licence are unpopulated everywhere, and the pointer that would have said so is dangling.
suggested_fix: Fix the path and add the missing families.

what: The catalog layer states FAOSTAT Emissions Totals was not retained and has no hash, while the raw manifest and the acquisition log show a held, hashed Pakistan extract acquired 2026-09-30 (30d22433..., 10,152 rows).
consequence: The benchmark rows still read the unhashed 2026-07-01 CO2e extract while a hashed native-gas-capable bulk sits beside it unused.
suggested_fix: Point the agriculture benchmarks at the held bulk and recover the native-gas columns, which would convert MC-01..MC-03 from an inversion to a direct read.

what: Licence status is inconsistent for the same publisher and sometimes inside one cell: EDGAR GHG booklet cc-by-4.0 but EDGAR v8.1 AP 'not-established'; UNFCCC 'unfccc-public' in public_documents.csv but 'undetermined' in source_documents rows 35/148/160; GEM CC-BY-4.0 in sources/GEM/GEM_SOURCES.json but 'undetermined' in source_documents rows 69 and 121, whose own note reads '(CC BY 4.0)'; SPAM CC-BY-4.0 in RICE_SOURCES.json but 'not-established' in assets.csv lines 266-268.
consequence: The per-product licence inventory is one of the four declared acceptance blockers; these contradictions are why it cannot be closed mechanically.
suggested_fix: Resolve to one value per publisher-product and test it.

what: Still registers the comparator as 'EDGAR (EDGAR_2024_GHG)', 'to ~2021', URL dataset_ghg2024, while the evidence layer uses the 2025 booklet to CY2024.

what: The row treats Climate TRACE as a partially independent check on plant GEOGRAPHY, but 29 of the 52 coordinates in data/sectors/power/activity/plant_coordinates.csv are themselves Climate TRACE derived (sources column: 13 'climatetrace', 16 'climatetrace+wri_gppd'). For those plants the check is circular.
evidence: value_counts of plant_coordinates.csv sources: wri_gppd 23, climatetrace+wri_gppd 16, climatetrace 13
consequence: 56% of the stations are checked against their own source. Agreement there is self-agreement and carries no evidence.
suggested_fix: Reclass to shared-upstream, and restrict the independent location claim to the 23 wri_gppd-only plants.

what: The fiscal-to-calendar approximation is applied inconsistently and is buried in free text. Most rows match FY2023-24 directly against a single CY2023 or CY2024 column with no blend; the transport and industry comparisons apply an explicit 0.5*CY(Y-1)+0.5*CY(Y) blend. The file has no column that states which treatment a row used.
consequence: A six-month overlap is silently treated as a year match in most rows. The size of that approximation is not stated anywhere a reader can see it.
suggested_fix: Add a period_approximation column with a closed vocabulary (direct | blend | fiscal-native) - matched_comparison.csv here carries one as a worked example.

what: Climate TRACE applies ONE intensity, 2431 g CO2e/kWh, to all 14 Pakistani coal plants (trace_g_per_kwh has exactly one distinct value for asset_type 'coal'). The gas classes are near-constant too. So CT's Pakistani power CO2 is activity x a per-fuel-class constant and carries no plant-specific intensity information. 2431 g/kWh is also roughly 2.5x any coal technology's plausible intensity.
evidence: groupby asset_type on trace_g_per_kwh: coal nunique=1, value 2431.0
consequence: Plant-level ratios trace_over_engine (1.51 to 9.89) are being read as a magnitude benchmark when the comparator can only test generation data. Any move toward this comparator would import a constant.
suggested_fix: State the constant-intensity limit on the product and stop quoting plant ratios as a magnitude check.

what: GEM assigns Engro Powergen Thar (24.8125 N, 70.3941 E), ThalNova (24.8155, 70.3884) and Thar Energy (24.8062, 70.4005) to district 'Thatta'. Those coordinates are in Tharparkar; Thatta is about 300 km west. Thar Coal Block-I, 11 km away, is correctly given as Tharparkar.
evidence: the file's own gem_district and coordinate columns
consequence: A comparator's district field disagrees with its own coordinates. Directly relevant to T-VAL-2's seven station conflicts.
suggested_fix: Use the coordinate, not GEM's district label, and record the conflict.
found_by: T-FIG-1 (found while reading the grid's peak cell)

what: The vocabulary is not comparable across periods. 113 streams are labelled 'static_structural' in FY2023-24 and 'reference_shape_backcast' in FY2015-16 - the same streams carrying the same weights. They are 50.0% of reference-year CO2 and 72.3% of reference-year CH4.
evidence: crosstab of spatial_time_basis between the two periods: static_structural(ref) x reference_shape_backcast(first) = 113 streams
consequence: A per-period tally of 'borrowed' weights undercounts the reference year, because the reference year's own borrowed weights are filed under a different name. Any trend read off this column is an artefact.
suggested_fix: Add a period-invariant flag (own-period evidence yes/no) beside the existing label. Panels (c) and (d) of fig_ghg_grid.pdf show both labels adjacent and say so in the legend title.

what: VERIFIED CORRECT, recorded because it is easy to get wrong when reading the cube: the comment says cells outside every district are _FillValue and an in-country zero is stored as 0. _FillValue is -9999.0 and masking is on by default, so np.nansum over the spatial_view axis silently converts out-of-country NaN to 0 and makes every cell look in-country. The figure script rebuilds the mask explicitly.
consequence: A consumer who uses nansum without rebuilding the mask will report 90,780 cells where there are 33,674.
suggested_fix: No product change needed; this is a consumer note.
